pollers.note: The distributed poller fleet. Each pool's nodes are polled by the pollers registered to it; a pool with no live poller goes unmonitored.
pollers.unavailable: Poller management is unavailable in skeleton mode.

empty.title: No pollers yet
empty.sub: Pollers appear here once they connect to the bus and send a heartbeat. Use Register poller for the remote-site setup snippet.

gaps.title: Recent monitoring gaps
gaps.note: Windows when core lost contact with a poller. A poller that stayed up but was cut off backfills its metrics for the window on reconnect; alerts are not backfilled (they resume from now).
gaps.passiveHint: Syslog, traps and flow exports arriving in this window were dropped — unlike polled metrics there is nothing to backfill from. SNMP informs are the exception: the sender retries until acknowledged.

nodes.title: Nodes polled by {{id}}
nodes.note: The working set core has published to this poller — what stops being monitored if it goes away.
nodes.empty: This poller holds no nodes right now.
nodes.offline: This poller is offline, so it holds no working set.
nodes.unknown: This core is a standby, so it does not track poller assignments.

remove.title: Remove poller
remove.confirmText: Remove poller {{id}} from the inventory? If it reconnects it will re-register automatically.

register.title: Register a poller
register.intro: Run a poller container at the remote site; it connects outbound to the central NATS bus. Fill in its identity below, then drop the generated <env>.env</env> next to <file>docker-compose.poller.yml</file> and bring it up.
register.invalidToken: Use letters, digits, dash or underscore only.
register.snippetEmpty: Enter a valid ID, pool and bus URL to generate the snippet.

pool.label: Pool
pool.hint: Nodes assigned to this pool are polled here.

busUrl.label: Bus URL
busUrl.hint: Include the poller credentials; a TLS URL is required off-site.

caFile.label: CA file path (optional)
caFile.hint: Only when the bus cert is signed by a private CA.

anchor.title: Anchor node for {{id}}
anchor.none: Work it out from the poller's own addresses
anchor.hint: The derived dependency graph takes its direction from how far each node is from a poller, so core needs to know where this poller sits. It normally works that out from the addresses the poller reports — but a poller in a container reports a container-network address that matches no monitored node, and then it has to be named here. Until every pool that has nodes has a placed poller, the derived graph cannot drive alert suppression.

err.anchor: failed to set the anchor node

health.note: Yagra's own health: the poll loop, its backing services, fleet data coverage, and host resources.

settings.note: System-wide monitoring defaults. Per-profile overrides take precedence over these.
settings.signInHint: Sign in with a config-management role to change this.

polling.title: Polling
polling.intervalHelp: How often each node is polled, unless its Device profile sets its own interval. {{min}}–{{max}} seconds.

err.range: Enter a whole number of seconds between {{min}} and {{max}}.

neighbors.title: Discovery walks
neighbors.note: What Yagra asks SNMP devices about the network around them, so the map and the dependency graph can be derived instead of typed in. All read-only: Yagra never configures a device.
neighbors.intervalHelp: How often each device is asked — currently {{cadence}}.

neighbors.name: Neighbors (CDP / LLDP)
neighbors.help: Which of this fleet's ports face which devices, with a history of when that changed. Turning this off stops the walks; everything already recorded is kept.

l3.name: Interface addresses
l3.help: Which IP prefixes each device has a foot in. This is what lets the network map derive links from shared subnets rather than from hand-entered parents.

arp.name: ARP / IPv6 neighbor cache
arp.help: Which hosts each router has actually spoken to — the only source that can name a device nobody has added yet. Off by default: this reads a table sized by the network rather than by the device, so it is the one walk that costs a busy switch measurable work. Results appear under Nodes ▸ Discovery.

routing.name: Routing adjacency (OSPF / BGP / routes)
routing.help: Which devices are peered or directly routed to each other — the links that share no subnet, such as a point-to-point /32, an unnumbered OSPF link, or an eBGP session. The routing table is never walked: it is asked about one destination at a time.

err.range: Enter a whole number of seconds between {{min}} and {{max}}.
err.rangeFor: {{walk}}: enter a whole number of seconds between {{min}} and {{max}}.
err.save: failed to save discovery walk settings

retention.title: Data retention
retention.note: How long each store keeps what. Lowering a window deletes data older than it on the next sweep. Two rows are set by a store's own start flag and cannot be changed from here.
retention.storeUnknown: Unknown — the store did not report a retention flag

err.range: {{name}}: enter a whole number between {{min}} and {{max}}.

integrations.note: Connect external systems monitored through a vendor cloud API.
integrations.unavailable: Integrations are unavailable in skeleton mode (no store).

meraki.desc: Read-only Dashboard API monitoring — availability, uplinks, and traffic across your Meraki organizations.

more.name: More integrations
more.desc: Additional vendor and notification integrations will appear here in a future release.

polling.title: Meraki polling
polling.hint: Global safeguard — instantly halt all Meraki Dashboard API polling fleet-wide, without deleting any organization config.

orgs.title: Organizations
orgs.empty: No Meraki organizations yet. Add one to start monitoring.

addOrg.title: Add Meraki organization
addOrg.apiKeyHint: Use a read-only Dashboard API key. It is sealed (encrypted at rest) and never shown again. Yagra only ever issues read-only GET calls to Meraki.
addOrg.selectHint: Select the organizations to monitor. All share this one API key.
addOrg.noOrgs: This key can't access any organizations.

networks.title: Network scope — {{name}}
networks.hint: Only monitored networks are collected. Un-checking a network stops narrowing API calls to it (existing device nodes are untouched — remove them to stop monitoring a device).
networks.empty: No networks yet — run “Import devices” to enumerate the org first.

cadence.title: Cadence — {{name}}
cadence.rateBudgetHint: Conservative — kept well under the org API cap so the customer keeps headroom.

delete.title: Delete organization
delete.confirmText: Delete {{name}}? Its imported device nodes, network scope, and HostTree groups are removed. Metric history in the TSDB is left. This cannot be undone.

import.title: Import devices — {{name}}
import.allImported: No new devices to import — every device this key can see is already monitored.

err.discover: failed to reach the Meraki API

bundle.pageNote: Move a monitoring configuration from one deployment to another. Admin only, in both directions.
bundle.notBackup: This is not a backup. A bundle carries no credentials, no notification-channel settings, no ingest tokens and no history — for disaster recovery take a database dump (see DEPLOYMENT.md, "Backup & restore").

export.title: Export
export.help: Download this deployment’s configuration as a single JSON file. Built-in profiles, metric sets and rules are left out — the target seeds its own.
export.err: Could not export the configuration bundle.

import.title: Import
import.help: Apply a bundle exported from another deployment. Rows with the same id are updated and new ones created; nothing is ever deleted.
import.warning: Applying this overwrites configuration that shares an id with a row in the bundle. Run the check first: it performs the real import and rolls it back, so the report is exactly what applying would do.

err.invalid-json: That file is not valid JSON.
err.not-a-bundle: That file is not a Yagra configuration bundle.
err.version: This bundle was written by a newer Yagra (bundle version {{version}}). Upgrade this deployment first.
err.failed: The import failed. Nothing was changed.

report.dryRun: Dry run — nothing was saved. Applying would create {{created}}, update {{updated}} and skip {{skipped}}.
report.noop: Nothing to do — this deployment already matches the bundle.

notes.skipped_builtin: Built-in rows were left out — the target seeds its own copies
notes.skipped_missing_reference: Skipped: something the row requires is not on this deployment
notes.reference_dropped: Imported, but a reference this deployment does not have was cleared
notes.secret_dropped_imported_disabled: A secret cannot be carried between deployments, so this arrives disabled unless one is already stored here — re-enter it, then enable
notes.webhook_token_reset: A webhook ingest token cannot be carried, so the source arrives disabled with an unusable token — rotate it to get a working one
notes.schedule_next_run_recomputed: The next run was recomputed from the cadence on this clock
